title: A scale position on the neck

cues.show: You with the guitar, the neck with the scale's notes on screen.
cues.say: This is the neck of the guitar with the notes of the scale on it. Each dot is a note to play.

cues.show: Point at the ringed notes, then tap a few dots.
cues.say: The ringed dots are the home note of the scale: name it. Tap a dot to hear that note.

cues.show: Press Play under the position and listen without playing.
cues.say: Press Play under the neck to hear the notes, from the lowest up to the highest and back down.

cues.show: Play it on the guitar, slowly, fretting hand visible.
cues.say: Now play it. Start on the lowest ringed note, play the dots on each string up to the thinnest string, then come back down the same way.

cues.show: Play it on the guitar, slowly, fretting hand visible.
cues.say: Use one finger for each fret, so your hand stays in one place.

cues.show: Play it again, looking away from the screen.
cues.say: Practice until your fingers find the dots without you looking at the screen.

cues.show: Play only the ringed notes. Then skip a note each time. Then a short line of your own.
cues.say: Try things with it. Play only the ringed notes and listen to how alike they sound.

cues.show: Play only the ringed notes. Then skip a note each time. Then a short line of your own.
cues.say: Play up the scale skipping every second note.

cues.show: Play only the ringed notes. Then skip a note each time. Then a short line of your own.
cues.say: Then pick three or four dots next to each other and make up a short line of your own. End it on a ringed note and hear how it sounds finished.
